To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel methodology to learn on graphs, in which we build a stack of Bayesian networks to learn a vertex's neighbourhood, and that we show how this methodology can be applied to graph classification and vertex labelling.

1) a stack of Bayesian networks can be used to learn representations for graph structured data, 2) the model can be trained on graphs without target labels, 3) the model can deal with both graph and vertex classification tasks.

(i) the use of contextual architectures for graph representation learning can be a powerful tool for the development of graph neural networks, (ii) the use of Bayesian networks in graph neural networks is a promising research direction, (iii) the performance of a graph neural network depends on the quality and quantity of training data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the study of contextual architectures for graph structured data, with benefits in term of context spreading and computational efficiency; (2) the study of how depth affects the model performances, and the critical analysis of some benchmark datasets used in the literature.
the following questions. How to build a deep graph neural network? How to learn from graphs without target labels? What is the role of depth in the context of graph learning?

the following questions: How can we build deeper graph convolutional architectures? How does the context spreading affect the performance of a graph model? What is the best way to train graph neural networks? How can we use graph neural networks without labels?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is a good choice for graph representation learning, especially in the case of large scale graphs.
the proposed method can be a valid alternative to graph convolutional networks in the absence of target labels, while being competitive in terms of performances.
our model outperforms all the baselines in most of the cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we introduce a novel methodology for probabilistic representation learning on graphs, with a theoretical foundation and a practical implementation, and that our experiments show that our model is a competitive alternative to neural architectures.
we introduce a new model for learning on graphs, which is able to deal with large scale data sets, and which can learn from data in an unsupervised fashion.

we propose an efficient and effective model for representation learning on graphs, with a novel approach for context spreading, which can be used as a general purpose model for graph data, without relying on target labels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the graph structure can be exploited in a probabilistic manner, without the need of labels.
the contextual architectures we propose are able to learn a richer set of features from the graph structure, and that this can be exploited to improve performances on graph classification tasks.
a deeper architecture, in terms of context, is a key factor for learning on graphs.
